# A patented siRNA entrant at the top of the lipid market

Novartis launched inclisiran in India in January 2024 as Sybrava, priced at
approximately **₹120,000 per injection**, and subsequently signed marketing
partnerships with three Indian companies - Mankind Pharma, JB Pharma and Lupin -
selling under the brands Crenzlo, Izirize and Tilpazan respectively. Reported
sales across the three partners were approximately **₹7.7 crore in the year from
April 2024**.

Inclisiran is a twice-yearly siRNA therapy that lowers LDL-C by roughly 50 per
cent in phase 3 trials. It is positioned as an add-on for patients who are
statin-intolerant or inadequately controlled, not as a statin replacement.

## Why this matters for prioritisation

This is a cautionary signal rather than an opportunity. The "Other Lipid
Reducers" sub-segment shows headline growth that partly reflects
innovator-controlled, patent-protected molecules. Growth in a space one cannot
legally enter is not an opportunity, and a prioritisation framework that ranks
on growth alone would flag it as a target.

Note also what the partner model implies: the commercially realistic route into
premium lipid innovation in India is **in-licensing**, not independent launch.
That is a strategic option worth naming, but it is a business-development
decision with a different risk profile from a generic combination launch.
